Siamese BERT Sentence Scorer

An autoencoder and Siamese BERT model scoring semantic textual similarity between augmented sentence pairs.

NLPBERTPyTorch

Overview

This project grew out of my master’s thesis at IASBS: given two sentences, produce a single score describing how semantically similar they are — even when one has been paraphrased, reordered, or lexically altered from the other. The approach was benchmarked against SBERT (Sentence-BERT) and Augmented SBERT baselines.

Method

A Siamese BERT encoder maps each sentence to a fixed-length embedding, and similarity is computed as the cosine of the two embeddings:

\[\text{sim}(a, b) = \frac{\mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{v}}{\lVert \mathbf{u} \rVert \, \lVert \mathbf{v} \rVert}\]

where $\mathbf{u} = \text{BERT}(a)$ and $\mathbf{v} = \text{BERT}(b)$ are the pooled sentence embeddings. An autoencoder is trained alongside the encoder to regularize the embedding space, minimizing reconstruction loss jointly with a similarity-scoring objective:

$$ \mathcal{L} = \mathcal{L}_{\text{sim}} + \lambda \, \mathcal{L}_{\text{recon}} $$

Result

The combined objective produced tighter, more separable embedding clusters than a similarity loss alone — augmented (paraphrased) pairs scored consistently higher than unrelated pairs across held-out validation sets.
